docs.title: Strategy
docs.text:
• Backend — integration-style tests through the public API (APITestCase), not the internal service classes, so they survive refactors. Written test-first: one failing behaviour test, then the smallest change that makes it pass. CI gates on ruff, ruff format, a missing-migration check, tests with coverage at or above 80%, check --deploy, and mypy strict.
  • Mobile — cubit tests for success, validation error and network failure, plus widget tests for the form. CI gates on dart format, flutter analyze --fatal-infos, and coverage at or above 25%.
  • UAT — a manual pass on staging before 29 Sep, following the checklist in each task plan.

docs.title: Running the suite locally
docs.text: config/settings.py calls load_dotenv(), so a local .env overrides the environment. api/test_security_settings.py (from #20) deletes DJANGO_DEBUG and PILAH_ALLOW_FAKE_GOOGLE_TOKEN and expects both to fall back to False, so it fails if a .env sets them. Pass the CI values as real environment variables instead of a .env when running the full suite.

docs.title: AI Literacy
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

AI used critically: its output verified, challenged and corrected, with the full prompt history published.

docs.title: How AI was used
docs.text:
• Tool: Claude Code as an agent in VS Code, working in the repository: reading code, running tests and checks, committing, and opening the PR.
  • Guardrails: the team's workspace skills (ship for the branch/worktree/PR workflow, tdd for red-green commits) and CI (ruff, mypy strict, coverage, SonarQube).
  • My role: deciding scope and priorities, relaying team decisions (stacking on #18, the rounding rule), approving outward actions (force-pushes, PR comments), and asking for verification before trusting results.

docs.title: 15–21 Sep — where verification changed the outcome
docs.text: Situation What verification found Asked to renumber the migration to 0012 before #18 merged It would reference a migration that did not exist yet (NodeNotFoundError) and break every test; we stacked on #18 instead "Re-check before making the PR" Confirmed the branch was current with staging, the diff held only the intended files, and no secrets were committed; found a second PR using the same migration number A test written after its fix Proved it catches the bug by disabling the fix and watching it fail An ordering bug that "seemed fine" Showed it was nondeterministic: 6 of 10 runs passed before the fix, 10 of 10 after Production environment values considered for local testing Not used: they would break tests and point local runs at the production database AI's claim that PR #22's rounding needed a PO decision Corrected after reading #22's code: the policy was already set there

docs.title: Example: correcting the AI's direction on rounding
docs.text:
Review finding 2 was about legacy saldo keeping its sen after a pencairan, while PR #22 rounds sen away on setoran. The AI's first recommendation was to wait: it framed the rounding as a decision for the PO, then suggested holding off until #22 merged, because the shared helper bulatkan_rupiah only exists on #22's branch.

I decided otherwise: the two money flows should be consistent now, and the sen dropped. The AI then:

  1. Implemented the decision without waiting for #22, using the same rule inline (ROUND_DOWN to whole rupiah), and explained why it did not create its own api/kalkulasi.py (it would conflict with #22's file).
  2. Wrote the failing test first ("RED as expected: the 50 sen survive") in 9b135b2, then the fix in 2981176.
  3. Checked that its rounding was identical to #22's (quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_DOWN)), so swapping in bulatkan_rupiah later changes nothing.

The follow-up is recorded publicly in the review thread: once #22 merges, the inline rounding is replaced with kalkulasi.bulatkan_rupiah.

docs.title: 22 Sep
docs.text: Situation What verification found All tests passed locally on SQLite CI on Postgres failed: a flush inside a transaction is rejected by Postgres. Diagnosed from the CI log and fixed in ad7d55f. Lesson: local SQLite is not proof; wait for CI A test failed after merging staging Diagnosed as a local .env artifact rather than "fixing" the test; confirmed by rerunning the way CI does "100% coverage" Separated precisely: 100% of my new code vs 90% of the project, measured by two tools that agree

docs.text:
Backend (#19):

docs.title: SonarQube, backend (pilah-be-staging)
docs.text:
• The server keeps one analysis per project, so the dashboard shows my most recent branch. It contains the week-1 backend code from #19 along with the later PIL-222 work.
  • None of the 14 open issues are mine. The Author facet attributes them to three other team members (9 + 3 + 2); my account does not appear.

docs.title: Gaps found in the analysis setup
docs.text:
1. Backend coverage misses config/. CI measures coverage with --source=api, but SonarQube also analyses config/, so config/ lines always show 0%. Changing CI to --source=api,config would make SonarQube's numbers accurate for the whole team.
  2. Mobile SonarQube analyses no code. Every mobile scan indexes the lib/ files (206 on #26) but logs 0 languages detected, so nothing is analysed and the project reports "no lines of code". The same holds on other team PRs, not just mine. The server has no Dart analysis, so for mobile the enforced static analysis is flutter analyze in CI. Fixing it needs Dart analysis enabled on the server.

docs.title: Why a self-hosted SonarQube
docs.text: The team runs its own SonarQube Community server (sonar.heraldoarman.com) instead of the cloud service because the cloud plan needs a paid subscription once a team has more than 5 members, and this team is larger than that. Self-hosting keeps the same analysis — CI reports every branch to it — at no cost.

Competency level: 3

Standard principles applied and shown in that week's code: single responsibility, a service layer, and extension without modifying existing consumers.

docs.title: Single Responsibility + DRY: BalanceService — 5447710
docs.text:
Two places computed a running saldo by summing setoran only: TransactionDetailSerializer.get_saldo_setelah_transaksi and the Excel export. Instead of fixing the formula twice, the rule "setoran added, pencairan subtracted" lives in one class, used by both.

api/services.py
class BalanceService:
    """Running saldo for a nasabah: setoran added, pencairan subtracted."""

    @staticmethod
    def saldo_at(
        bank_sampah: BankSampah, nasabah_id: UUID, until: datetime, until_id: UUID
    ) -> Decimal:
        setoran = Transaksi.objects.filter(bank_sampah=bank_sampah, nasabah_id=nasabah_id).filter(
            Q(tanggal__lt=until) | Q(tanggal=until, id__lte=until_id)
        )
        # At an equal tanggal a pencairan is ordered after the setoran, so it is
        # excluded here; the export's merge below applies the same rule.
        pencairan = Pencairan.objects.filter(
            bank_sampah=bank_sampah, nasabah_id=nasabah_id, tanggal__lt=until
        )
        masuk = setoran.aggregate(total=Coalesce(Sum("total_nilai"), Decimal("0.00")))["total"]
        keluar = pencairan.aggregate(total=Coalesce(Sum("nominal"), Decimal("0.00")))["total"]
        return cast(Decimal, masuk - keluar)

The serializer is then one line, and the export applies the same ordering rule in its own running-total pass:

api/serializers.py
return BalanceService.saldo_at(obj.bank_sampah, obj.nasabah_id, obj.tanggal, obj.id)

The payoff came with review finding 3: the tie-break at an equal tanggal was wrong, and fixing it meant changing one rule in one place (765f90f) instead of hunting for every place a saldo was summed.

docs.title: Service layer: PencairanService — fbab07b
docs.text:
The business rule (lock the nasabah and saldo rows, check the saldo, record, deduct) sits in PencairanService.create_pencairan, not in the view. The whole operation is one atomic transaction, so a failure anywhere leaves neither a record nor a changed saldo.

api/services.py
class PencairanService:
    @staticmethod
    @transaction.atomic
    def create_pencairan(user: User, payload: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Pencairan:
        bank = user.bank_sampah
        assert bank is not None  # ponytail: views gate on IsActivePengelola
        nasabah = (
            Nasabah.objects.select_for_update()
            .filter(
                id=payload["nasabah_id"],
                bank_sampah=bank,
                is_active=True,
                status=Nasabah.Status.APPROVED,
            )
            .first()
        )
        if not nasabah:
            raise serializers.ValidationError(
                {"nasabah_id": ["Nasabah tidak ditemukan atau tidak aktif"]}
            )

        saldo, _ = Saldo.objects.select_for_update().get_or_create(nasabah=nasabah)
        nominal = payload["nominal"]
        saldo_sebelum = saldo.total_saldo
        if nominal > saldo_sebelum:
            raise serializers.ValidationError({"nominal": ["Saldo nasabah tidak mencukupi"]})
        ...

The view stays thin: validate, delegate, respond. It holds no business rule at all, following the existing TransactionService.create_setoran pattern.

api/views.py
    def create(self, request: Request) -> Response:
        serializer = PencairanCreateSerializer(data=request.data)
        serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=True)
        pencairan = PencairanService.create_pencairan(_user(request), serializer.validated_data)
        return Response(PencairanDetailSerializer(pencairan).data, status=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)

Because the saldo check happens inside the locked transaction, two simultaneous payouts cannot both pass it — the second waits for the row lock and then sees the reduced saldo.

docs.title: Open/Closed in practice: a separate Pencairan model — fbab07b
docs.text:
Adding a PENCAIRAN type to Transaksi with a negative value would have forced changes in every consumer that assumes a transaksi has items: the list serializer, export, dashboard and WhatsApp notifier. A new model extends the system without modifying them.

api/models.py
class Pencairan(TimestampedModel):
    class Metode(models.TextChoices):
        TUNAI = "tunai", "Tunai"
        TRANSFER = "transfer", "Transfer"

    nasabah = models.ForeignKey(Nasabah, on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="pencairan")
    bank_sampah = models.ForeignKey(BankSampah, on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="pencairan")
    dicatat_oleh = models.ForeignKey(
        User, on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="pencairan_dicatat"
    )
    nominal = models.DecimalField(max_digits=14, decimal_places=2)
    metode = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=Metode.choices)
    # Receipt snapshots at record time; PIL-230 decides how edits affect them.
    saldo_sebelum = models.DecimalField(max_digits=14, decimal_places=2)
    saldo_sesudah = models.DecimalField(max_digits=14, decimal_places=2)

    class Meta:
        db_table = "pencairan"
        ordering = ["-tanggal"]
        indexes = [models.Index(fields=["bank_sampah", "nasabah", "tanggal"])]
        constraints = [
            models.CheckConstraint(
                condition=models.Q(nominal__gt=0), name="pencairan_nominal_positive"
            ),
        ]

PROTECT on all three foreign keys keeps a money record from losing the nasabah, bank or pengurus it refers to, and the check constraint enforces a positive nominal in the database as well as in the serializer. The trade-off is documented in the PR description and the task plan.

docs.title: Consistency with existing rules — 49cd153
docs.text:
Review finding 1 was that pencairan accepted any active nasabah, while setoran already required an approved membership — so a pending member could be paid out but not deposit. The fix makes both money flows resolve the nasabah the same way:

api/services.py — identical in create_setoran and create_pencairan

            .filter(
                id=payload["nasabah_id"],
                bank_sampah=bank,
                is_active=True,
                status=Nasabah.Status.APPROVED,
            )
            .first()

One rule, applied on both sides, rather than a second variation of "who may transact".

docs.title: Removing dead code — bd38dc6
docs.text:
PencairanViewSet.list had an unpaginated fallback that could never run, because StandardPagination is the global default, so paginate_queryset never returns None. Six lines became two, and the reason is written down so the next reader does not restore the branch:

api/views.py — bd38dc6
     def list(self, request: Request) -> Response:
-        qs = self.get_queryset()
-        page = self.paginate_queryset(qs)
-        serializer = PencairanDetailSerializer(page if page is not None else qs, many=True)
-        if page is not None:
-            return self.get_paginated_response(serializer.data)
-        return Response(serializer.data)
+        # Pagination is configured globally (PAGE_SIZE), so a page always exists.
+        page = self.paginate_queryset(self.get_queryset())
+        return self.get_paginated_response(PencairanDetailSerializer(page, many=True).data)

The list test stayed green, which is what made the deletion safe rather than hopeful.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Competency level: 1

Code prevents OWASP A01 (Broken Access Control) and A04 (Insecure Design), each control guarded by a test.

docs.title: The two controls in code
docs.text:
Every pencairan endpoint carries the permission class, and every query is rooted at the caller's own bank sampah, taken from the session rather than from the request body:

api/views.py
class PencairanViewSet(viewsets.GenericViewSet):
    permission_classes = [IsActivePengelola]
    serializer_class = PencairanDetailSerializer

    def get_queryset(self) -> QuerySet[Pencairan]:
        qs = Pencairan.objects.filter(bank_sampah=_bank_sampah(self.request)).select_related(
            "nasabah", "bank_sampah", "dicatat_oleh"
        )

_bank_sampah reads the bank off the authenticated user, so a caller cannot name someone else's bank:

api/views.py
def _bank_sampah(request: Request) -> BankSampah:
    bank = _user(request).bank_sampah
    assert bank is not None  # ponytail: IsActivePengelola guarantees bank membership
    return bank

Because the filter is part of the base queryset, retrieve on another bank's pencairan finds nothing and returns 404 rather than 403 — the record's existence is never confirmed.

api/tests.py — test_pencairan_detail_is_scoped_to_bank_sampah
        self.assertEqual(
            self.client.get(f"/api/v1/pencairan/{created.data['id']}").status_code, 404
        )
        ...
        self.assertEqual(self.client.post("/api/v1/pencairan", {}, format="json").status_code, 403)

        self.client.credentials()
        self.assertEqual(self.client.post("/api/v1/pencairan", {}, format="json").status_code, 401)

No mass assignment: the write serializer accepts five fields and nothing else. bank_sampah, dicatat_oleh, status and both saldo snapshots are set by the service, so a crafted request body cannot book a payout against another bank or forge a receipt.

api/serializers.py
class PencairanCreateSerializer(serializers.Serializer[Any]):
    nasabah_id = serializers.UUIDField(required=True)
    nominal = serializers.DecimalField(max_digits=14, decimal_places=2, required=True)
    metode = serializers.ChoiceField(choices=Pencairan.Metode.choices, required=True)
    tanggal = serializers.DateTimeField(required=False)
    keterangan = serializers.CharField(
        required=False, allow_blank=True, allow_null=True, max_length=255
    )

The money rules are enforced twice, in the serializer and again in the database:

api/serializers.py
    def validate_nominal(self, value: Decimal) -> Decimal:
        if value <= 0:
            raise serializers.ValidationError("Nominal harus lebih dari nol")
        if value != value.to_integral_value():
            raise serializers.ValidationError("Nominal harus dalam rupiah bulat tanpa desimal")
        return value
api/models.py
        constraints = [
            models.CheckConstraint(
                condition=models.Q(nominal__gt=0), name="pencairan_nominal_positive"
            ),
        ]

And the A04 control — the saldo check runs inside the same locked transaction that writes the record, so two concurrent payouts cannot both pass it:

api/services.py
        saldo, _ = Saldo.objects.select_for_update().get_or_create(nasabah=nasabah)
        nominal = payload["nominal"]
        saldo_sebelum = saldo.total_saldo
        if nominal > saldo_sebelum:
            raise serializers.ValidationError({"nominal": ["Saldo nasabah tidak mencukupi"]})

docs.title: Concepts applied this week
docs.text: # Concept Applied in Evidence 1 End-to-end testing of Flutter web through its semantics tree, with assertions. Flutter web draws on a canvas, so a browser tool can only reach it through the accessibility (semantics) layer. Last week I only explored this: screenshots, nothing asserted. This week the checks wait on labels instead of fixed pauses, assert outcomes, measure where elements sit, and handle labels that Flutter merges into one node. PIL-341 slice 3 (#127), and both QA fixes (#153, #154), at desktop and phone sizes against a local build and backend #127, #153, #154 (E2E tables and screenshots in each description) 2 Client-side routing state, and route parameters as untrusted input. In go_router, push doesn't write to the browser URL unless optionURLReflectsImperativeAPIs is on, so "survives a refresh" means something different for pushed and go routes. And a value read from the URL that ends up in an API path can steer the user's own authenticated requests elsewhere, unless it is validated. #127: a saved draft opens from ?id=, and only a bare id is accepted (OWASP A01, A03). The refresh limitation was documented for the lead dev rather than worked around app-wide. a491758, 7d938f9, Security

    • They surfaced a desktop dialog whose title never reaches the semantics tree. That is recorded as INFO, a likely accessibility gap, rather than marked as a pass.
  • Treating route parameters as input changed a feature I had planned as a convenience (open a draft from its link) into one with a guard. The test sends ../nasabah, d-1/konfirmasi and a space, and asserts that no request is built from them. Learning how push and the URL interact also stopped me from promising a refresh behaviour the app's router doesn't give.

docs.title: How AI was used this week
docs.text:
• Tool: Claude Code as an agent in VS Code across pilah-be, pilah-mobile and pilah-docs, Linear through Composio, GitHub through gh, and the SonarQube CLI and the SonarCloud API for coverage.
  • Guardrails:
    • the workspace skills (ship, tdd, ask-for-review);

    • rules kept in memory: phase-tagged commits, replying inside review threads, never merging base branches into stacked ones without asking.

docs.title: Where verification changed the outcome
docs.text: Situation What happened 11 Oct: It offered "a button in the expanded card" as the entry point for the price history, and I picked it On reading the page, it found the card wasn't expandable: tapping it opens the edit sheet. It told me its option had been based on a wrong premise, then put the button in the card's info column, the closest match to my choice. 11 Oct: SonarCloud showed #62/#73 a few lines short of 100%, all in generated code I said to always cover 100%, generated or not. Rather than add an exclusion, it traced why lcov skipped the file, and found that the graph CI builds would crash the app on launch. 11 Oct: Its first check of that crash passed It noticed build_runner had skipped regenerating the file and left the hand-edited copy in place, so the check proved nothing. It deleted the file, regenerated it, and only then reported the crash, with the exact error. 11 Oct: The crash fix touched the team's CI and a teammate's code It stopped and asked how to land it (separate PR, inside #62, or just report it) before changing shared workflows. 12 Oct: Tristan's 8 review notes Each was checked against the code before anything changed. All 8 held up. One (the Sonar exclusion) showed that staging had moved since the branch was cut. 12 Oct: "Can we use stacked PRs for #79 and #92?" #92 was already stacked, so the question was ambiguous. It also checked its saved rule against merging a base branch into a stacked one. It asked which stack shape I meant, then used a revert plus cherry-pick -x, not a force-push, so last week's evidence links stay valid. 12 Oct: #74's crash fix became redundant when Tristan's #71 landed the same change It took staging's version in the conflict and rewrote the PR around what was still new, instead of keeping a duplicate fix. 13 Oct: I asked whether Playwright meant I wouldn't need manual tests It answered "partly". It said its own run had only taken screenshots and asserted nothing, so it was visual QA and not a test suite, and that its fixed pauses were the fragile style I hoped to avoid. Then it listed what automation can't cover. Screenshots below. 13 Oct: "Do it for future commits and PRs" It saved the rule, then asked where the checks should run instead of deciding itself. Its recommendation was a CI job with the API stubbed, which would touch the team's pipeline. I chose local only, and it rewrote the rule to match. It also noticed that an earlier rule (100% coverage) had been saved without an index entry, so future sessions would not have loaded it, and fixed that. 16 Oct: Reviewing Ghani's #104 Three candidate findings were checked before posting. The CI coverage change was measured with and without tests/ (99% either way), so it was dropped. The alternative to the spreadsheet escaping was tried and turned out worse, so it was dropped too. The performance suggestion went in only after a benchmark showed the same result from fewer queries.

docs.title: Example: covering generated code turned up a crash
docs.text:
The obvious response to "97.4% on SonarCloud, the gap is generated code" is an exclusion line in sonar.yml. Instead:

  1. The cause. It checked why the file was missing from lcov: the generator writes // coverage:ignore-file.
  2. The proposal. It proposed resolving every registration in a test.
  3. The finding. Building that test exposed that the graph CI generates asks for a bool nobody registers. Every CI-built app would crash on launch, and nobody had noticed, because flutter run uses the hand-edited copy.
  4. My decision. Before touching shared CI and a teammate's bloc, it laid out three ways to land the fix and waited for my choice.

The result is pilah-mobile #74, which keeps that class of crash out of future builds.

docs.title: Example: Playwright is not a replacement for manual testing
docs.text:
On 13 Oct the agent ran PIL-341 slice 2 in a local web build with Playwright and took desktop and phone screenshots. That run caught a dialog with square corners, which the widget tests had missed. I had only just heard of Playwright, so I asked about it before relying on it.

1. "So I don't need manual tests?" It didn't just agree. It said what its own run had been: a script that clicked through the flow and saved screenshots, with nothing asserted, so scripted visual QA, not automated testing. It confirmed my point about auto-waiting, with a catch for Flutter: Flutter web draws on a canvas, which is why its script had fallen back on fixed waitForTimeout pauses, the fragile style I wanted to avoid.

2. "Can't we just use the semantics tree?" It explained that, on the web, the semantics tree is the accessibility layer, and why it is off by default. It gave two ways to turn it on, a flag in the app for E2E builds only or a click in the test, and recommended stable Semantics(identifier:) selectors over matching visible text.

3. "Do it for future commits and PRs." It saved the rule, then asked where the tests should run. It recommended CI with the API stubbed, and I chose local only. The saved rule says that for every web UI PR the scripts walk the flow and assert the result, wait on labels instead of fixed pauses, and save desktop and phone screenshots for the PR description. It also promised to rerun the slice 2 flows the new way and add the results to #84.

What changed. I came in thinking a new tool would replace a practice. I left with a rule that says what the tool checks and what it doesn't, and that rule is now in the agent's memory for every later web PR. This is the same pattern as earlier weeks' rules (phase-tagged commits, 100% coverage), kept as notes that change how later sessions work.

The section below is what #74 changes.

docs.title: Raising the bar: measuring generated code
docs.text:
SonarCloud put #62 at 97.4% and #73 at 96.2%. Every uncovered line was a registration in the generated lib/services/di.config.dart. Generated or not, it is code that ships, so I covered it rather than explaining it away.

Why it was invisible:

  • injectable_generator marks the file // coverage:ignore-file, so lcov leaves it out.
  • sonar.yml also excluded it from analysis.

What covering it found: the graph CI builds could not create AuthenticationBloc, because it asked dependency injection for a bool nobody registers. app.dart creates that bloc at start-up, so CI-built apps would crash on launch. Local flutter run hid it, because it uses a hand-maintained copy of the file.

The fix, pilah-mobile #74:

  • A full-graph test. di_graph_test builds every registration in dev and prod, and fails when a new registration is missing from its list.
  • Coverage in CI. CI and SonarCloud now measure the file: the marker is dropped after code generation (941f24d), and the Sonar exclusion is removed, as Tristan asked in review (26fcf40).
  • Result: every executable line of the file is covered.
  • Docs. AGENTS.md now says how the generated file is committed and tested.

The crash itself reached staging first through Tristan's #71 (the same @ignoreParam fix), so #74 keeps staging's version of the bloc.

docs.title: Automated checks, all passing

docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Six new merge requests this week:

  • PIL-331 on both repositories;

docs.title: Programming
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Standard principles applied and shown in this week's code:

  • SOLID: single responsibility, open/closed and dependency inversion. See SOLID in this week's code.
  • One rule for a price version's status, the same order the setoran lookup uses.
  • Money kept exact on mobile, without double.
  • A stale-response guard against a list-reload race.
  • Seed data written through the one approved write path.

Each item names the design issue it addresses, the pattern or principle used, and its type. The GoF design patterns (Singleton, Adapter, Observer, and loosely Command) have their own section. Three of the issues were in my own code and were found in Tristan's review; the table says which.

docs.title: Design issues and the patterns that address them
docs.text:
Code Design issue Pattern / principle Type Origin Version status Two readers of the price history (the history screen and the setoran price lookup) that must never disagree; a status that could depend on where a page breaks Consistent ordering invariant: both use the same order (start, then id), and the status is computed over the whole history before pagination Principle (domain invariant) Designed in (PIL-331) Money Primitive obsession with floating point for money: 3333.99 read through double and toInt() showed a price that was never stored Money in minor units: the price is an integer number of sen, parsed from the decimal string without a float Technique (minor units) Defect in my code, Tristan's review of #73 Stale response Race condition on out-of-order async responses: an older reload answering last overwrote the newer price Request sequence token ("latest request wins"): each reload is numbered and a stale answer is dropped Technique (concurrency) Defect in my code, Tristan's review of #62 Seed data Bypassing the domain's write path: the seed wrote price versions itself and priced old setoran at today's rate, so its rules could drift from the app's (BR-03) Service layer as the single write path: every price goes through catat_harga, and each setoran is priced at its own date Architectural (PoEAA Service Layer) Defect in my code, Tristan's review of #79 (and) Single responsibility A fat view mixing HTTP with business rules SRP: the rule is a plain port function; the serializer shapes, the view wires Principle (SOLID) Designed in (PIL-331) Open/closed Changing PIL-304's working POST action to add a read OCP: @ubah_harga.mapping.get adds the read without editing the action Principle (SOLID) Designed in (PIL-331) Dependency inversion A cubit coupled to the HTTP client, untestable without a server Repository pattern + use case, injected (DIP): the cubit sees only the use case and the HargaRepository interface Principle (SOLID) + Architectural (Repository) Designed in (PIL-331) Don't repeat yourself Duplicated code: my first version copied another page's private date formatter Extract function into one tested shared helper Principle (DRY) Caught in my own [REFACTOR] commit

Type says what kind of solution each one is. Only part of it is a GoF design pattern (creational, structural, behavioural). The rest are principles (SOLID, DRY), architectural patterns from Fowler's Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture (PoEAA), or plain techniques. The GoF patterns that do appear in this week's code are listed in GoF design patterns in this week's code.

docs.title: PIL-331 — the price history, and the review round (10–12 Oct)
One rule for a version's status — 601b948, f0b6b0d
docs.text:
The history marks each version terjadwal, berlaku, sebelumnya or digantikan. The rule uses the same order as harga_berlaku (start, then id), so the screen can never disagree with the price a setoran uses. It runs over the whole history before pagination, so a page break can't change a status:

apps/waste_catalog/api.py
def susun_riwayat_harga(jenis: JenisSampah, pada: datetime) -> list[VersiHarga]:
    riwayat: list[VersiHarga] = []
    di_atasnya: HargaSampah | None = None
    sudah_ada_yang_berlaku = False
    for versi in jenis.riwayat_harga.select_related("dibuat_oleh").order_by(
        "-berlaku_mulai", "-id"
    ):
        status: StatusVersi
        if di_atasnya is not None and versi.berlaku_mulai == di_atasnya.berlaku_mulai:
            status = "digantikan"
        elif versi.berlaku_mulai > pada:
            status = "terjadwal"
        elif not sudah_ada_yang_berlaku:
            status = "berlaku"
            sudah_ada_yang_berlaku = True
        else:
            status = "sebelumnya"
        riwayat.append(VersiHarga(versi, status))
        di_atasnya = versi
    return riwayat

digantikan exists because correcting a scheduled price is a new version with the same start (PIL-304's append-only rule). Without it, the history would show two scheduled prices for one day.

Design issue: two readers of one history that must agree. Pattern: a consistent ordering invariant, computed before pagination. Origin: designed in.

docs.title: Money kept exact — 4226ca5
docs.text:
Design issue: primitive obsession with floating point for money. Pattern: money in minor units (integer sen). Origin: a defect in my code, found in Tristan's review.

Tristan's review found that the mobile model read 3333.99 through double and toInt(), showing a price that was never stored. A version now holds its price in sen, and the backend's decimal string is cut, not parsed as a float, so no binary rounding can creep in:

lib/features/harga/data/models/versi_harga_model.dart
int _keSen(String angka) {
  final bagian = angka.split('.');
  final sen = (bagian.length > 1 ? bagian[1] : '').padRight(2, '0');
  return (int.tryParse(bagian[0]) ?? 0) * 100 +
      (int.tryParse(sen.substring(0, 2)) ?? 0);
}

docs.title: A stale response can't win — bd21f70
docs.text:
Design issue: a race condition on out-of-order async responses. Pattern: a request sequence token, so the latest request wins. Origin: a defect in my code, found in Tristan's review.

Saving a price change reloads the list twice: after the PUT and after the price POST. If the first GET answered last, the old price came back. Each reload is now numbered, and an answer is dropped once a newer reload has started:

lib/features/harga/presentation/cubit/harga_cubit.dart
  Future<void> loadHarga({bool silent = false}) async {
    final permintaan = ++_permintaanTerakhir;
    if (!silent || state is! HargaLoaded) emit(HargaLoading());
    final result = await getHargaUseCase.execute();
    // Reload yang lebih baru sudah berjalan: jawaban ini sudah usang.
    if (permintaan != _permintaanTerakhir) return;
    ...

docs.title: Seed data follows the same rules — f67a84f, dc29a68
docs.text:
Design issue: bypassing the domain's write path, so the seed's rules could drift from the app's. Pattern: the service layer as the single write path. Origin: a defect in my code, found in Tristan's review.

The seed command wrote price versions itself and priced historical setoran at today's rate, so rerunning it after a price change rewrote old totals. It now writes through catat_harga, the one approved write path in AGENTS.md, and prices each setoran at its own date (BR-03).

docs.title: GoF design patterns in this week's code
docs.text:
All four are in PIL-331's mobile side (pilah-mobile #73), in code I wrote. They follow the app's existing Clean Architecture layout.

Category Pattern Where What it does here Creational Singleton (container-managed) GetRiwayatHargaUseCase (@lazySingleton), 35e908a The injection container builds one shared instance on first use. A variant of GoF Singleton: the container, not the class, guarantees the single instance, so a test can still pass a stub. Structural Adapter HargaRepositoryImpl.getRiwayatHarga, 7077e55 Adapts the data source, which throws exceptions and reads paginated JSON, to the domain's HargaRepository interface, which returns Either<NetworkException, List<VersiHarga>>. Behavioural Observer RiwayatHargaCubit → BlocBuilder on RiwayatHargaPage, 35e908a, cd41645 The cubit emits a new state, and every subscribed widget rebuilds. The cubit doesn't know who is listening. Behavioural Command (loosely) GetRiwayatHargaUseCase implements UseCase<List<VersiHarga>, String>, 35e908a Each use case is one request wrapped in an object behind a uniform interface, so the cubit calls it without knowing how the request is carried out. There is no undo or queue, so it is only loosely Command. lib/features/harga/data/repositories/harga_repository_impl.dart (Adapter)
  Future<Either<NetworkException, List<VersiHarga>>> getRiwayatHarga(
      String id) async {
    try {
      return Right(await remoteDataSource.getRiwayatHarga(id));
    } on Exception catch (e) {
      return Left(NetworkException.handleException(e));
    }
  }
lib/features/harga/presentation/pages/riwayat_harga_page.dart (Observer)
      body: BlocBuilder<RiwayatHargaCubit, RiwayatHargaState>(

Two names to avoid mixing up. Python's @ubah_harga.mapping.get on the backend is a language decorator, not the GoF Decorator pattern. Repository and Service Layer are PoEAA patterns, not GoF.

docs.title: Single responsibility — 601b948
docs.text:
The status rule is a plain function in the catalog's port (above), with no HTTP in it. The serializer only shapes a row, and the view only wires the lookup to pagination:

apps/waste_catalog/views.py
    @ubah_harga.mapping.get
    def riwayat_harga(self, request: Request, pk: str | None = None) -> Response:
        page = self.paginate_queryset(susun_riwayat_harga(self.get_object(), timezone.now()))
        return self.get_paginated_response(VersiHargaSerializer(page, many=True).data)

@ubah_harga.mapping.get adds the read on the same path as PIL-304's POST, without changing that action: open/closed.

docs.title: Dependency inversion — 35e908a
docs.text:
RiwayatHargaCubit knows only the use case, which knows only the HargaRepository interface. Tests swap the whole HTTP layer for a stub (StubApi) without touching the cubit:

lib/features/harga/presentation/cubit/riwayat_harga_cubit.dart
@injectable
class RiwayatHargaCubit extends Cubit<RiwayatHargaState> {
  final GetRiwayatHargaUseCase _getRiwayat;

  RiwayatHargaCubit(this._getRiwayat) : super(const RiwayatHargaState());

docs.title: Don't repeat yourself — 2eb1bea
docs.text:
Design issue: duplicated code. Pattern: extract function into a shared, tested helper. Origin: my own first version, fixed in its [REFACTOR] commit.

The history screen first copied the pencairan revision page's private date-and-time formatter. The refactor moved it to one tested formatTanggalJamId, and both screens call it.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

A dynamic security scan of the backend with Metasploit Framework 6.5.3, explained, with a test-first patch plan: Security scan report. The scan was run against my own local instance and cross-checked against python manage.py check --deploy.

Alongside the scan, this week's new code guards A01 Broken Access Control on the new price-history endpoint (named in its commit and tested), with two more OWASP behaviours (A08, A09) tested but not named in their commits.

docs.title: Security scan (level 3)
docs.text:
Ran Metasploit against the backend on a local instance (manage.py runserver, seeded test DB; staging and production were not touched). Method: Metasploit auxiliary/scanner/http/* for fingerprinting, headers, directory enumeration and method discovery, then curl to verify, then check --deploy as a static cross-check.

Explained — why a generic exploit framework finds little here. Metasploit exploits known vulnerabilities in known software. PILAH's backend is a bespoke Django/DRF app, so no exploit module matches it; its scanners confirmed there is no exploitable off-the-shelf service, and the findings that matter are application- and configuration-level. That clean result is itself a finding.

Findings (full detail and evidence in the report):

# Finding OWASP Severity Scope 1 /api/schema/ and /api/docs/ served without authentication — full API contract disclosed A01 / A05 Medium prod + dev 2 HSTS not configured (SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS unset; security.W004) A05 Low–Med prod 3 App-layer HTTPS redirect not enforced (security.W008) A05 Low prod 4 No Content-Security-Policy / Permissions-Policy A05 Low prod + dev 5 Server banner leaks framework and Python version A05 Info dev 6 DEBUG=true error pages leak the URL configuration A05 Med if deployed dev-only

Patch plan (priority first), each a test-first change naming its OWASP category:

  1. Restrict the schema/docs behind IsAdminUser (or IsAuthenticated), so an unauthenticated request gets 401/403.
  2. Enable HSTS (SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS, include-subdomains, preload) guarded by not DEBUG.
  3. SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT = not DEBUG, using the proxy header already set.
  4. Add a minimal CSP / Permissions-Policy, scoped to the API and the Swagger page.
  5. Suppress the Server banner at the gunicorn/middleware layer.
  6. A CI/start-up guard that a production build cannot boot with DEBUG=true.

What held up. Every /api/v1/* endpoint returns 401 without a token; /admin/ redirects to login; X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy and COOP are all present; /.env is 404, there is no path traversal, and only safe HTTP methods are allowed.

docs.text: OWASP category Guard Commit Named in the commit A01 Broken Access Control Only the owning bank's pengurus can read a jenis's price history 8bc2be8 yes A08 Software and Data Integrity Failures Rerunning the seed no longer rewrites historical setoran snapshots 857735b → f67a84f no A09 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures The price history shows who recorded each version 1f43102 → 50d9392 no

docs.title: A01 · Broken Access Control
docs.text:
PIL-331's GET /jenis-sampah/{id}/harga exposes every past price of a jenis — business data — so I checked it against the two ways it could leak:

apps/waste_catalog/test_riwayat_harga.py (excerpt)
        self.auth_as(pengurus_lain)
        self.assertEqual(self.riwayat(jenis["id"]).status_code, 404)
        self.auth_as(nasabah)
        self.assertEqual(self.riwayat(jenis["id"]).status_code, 403)

The action reuses the viewset's bank-scoped get_object and IsActivePengelola, so the test passed when written. I proved it guards something by swapping in an unscoped lookup, seeing another bank read the prices and the test fail, then restoring the code. The commit names the category: "(OWASP A01, BR-01)".

docs.title: Also tested this week
docs.text:
• A08, data integrity. Each seeded setoran must keep the price of its own date (BR-03). The red test recorded a price change taking effect now and reran the seed; a historical snapshot went from 3,500 to 99,999. The fix prices each setoran at its stored tanggal.
  • A09, audit trail. The price history makes dibuat_oleh readable to the pengurus (null for prices backfilled by the migration).

docs.title: Test Driven Development
docs.text:
Competency level: 4

Level 3 met: PIL-331 was built test-first on both sides, with [RED]/[GREEN]/[REFACTOR] in every commit subject. Every review finding Tristan raised was fixed the same way, with a failing test first. Changed lines are 100% covered in every MR, generated code included, and each behaviour is tested with positive, negative and corner cases.

Level 4: advanced testing methods in the commits:

  • Mocks, stubs and fakes for isolation: mocktail, Completers that decide which request answers first, and a fake backend at the HTTP boundary.
  • Mutation checks: tests that passed when written were proven to guard their code by breaking the code and watching them fail.
  • Full-graph test: a test builds the app's whole generated dependency graph in both environments.

SonarCloud showed #62 and #73 a few lines short of 100%. Every missing line was a registration in the generated di.config.dart, which the generator marks coverage:ignore-file. docs.title: Advanced testing methods
docs.text:
• Controlled ordering with Completers (#62). The race test hands the cubit two pending requests, answers the newer one first and the older one last, and checks the newer price stays.
  • A fake backend at the HTTP boundary (#73). StubApi replaces Dio's adapter, so the real data source, repository, use case and cubit run against canned responses. Failures are injected at the transport level (api.fail).
  • Mutation checks (#92, #73).
    • For the three pinned backend tests, I broke the code they guard and watched each fail.
    • For the unknown-status fallback (5123002), I replaced the fallback with a hard lookup and watched the test fail.
  • Full-graph resolution (#74). di_graph_test builds every registration of the generated dependency graph. It's the test that would have caught the startup crash before a build shipped.

docs.title: Team Development Management
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Two detailed reviews of teammates' merge requests, each with feasible improvement suggestions:

  • Gabriel's PIL-354 (pilah-be #97, 13 Oct). Two inline suggestions. Gabriel took both, and built a source-level guard on the first one.
  • Ghani's PIL-248 (pilah-be #104, 16 Oct). One performance suggestion, measured against the current code before posting: same result, 5 queries down to 3, 91 ms down to 34 ms.

The other side of reviewing is here too:

  • Tristan's 8 findings on my merge requests: each verified against the code, fixed test-first and answered in its thread.
  • A crash that every CI-built app would have hit on launch, found and raised.

docs.title: Review given: Gabriel's pilah-be #97 (PIL-354), 13 Oct
docs.text:
PIL-354 fixes CORS for the web dashboard. It allows the Idempotency-Key request header and exposes Content-Disposition, so browser downloads get their filename. Gabriel added a registry of custom headers in shared_kernel/http_headers.py, which both the CORS settings and the views are meant to read from.

Review (approved) · inline: registry constant, test that can't fail

Before commenting, I checked that the registry covers everything that crosses origins. Idempotency-Key is the only custom header the API reads, and pilah-mobile sends nothing outside the default allowed set. Content-Disposition is written in four places, and the one exposed header covers all of them, including the draft-pencairan export that my PIL-341 web work uses.

Suggestion Why it matters What Gabriel did (14 Oct) Use the registry constant where the header is written. The docstring says the CORS setting and the code share one value. That held for Idempotency-Key, but the four writes of Content-Disposition still spelled the name out (ledger/views.py L151, L372, L384, nasabah/home.py L243) It makes the docstring's claim true for both lists, and gives the next response header an obvious place to be registered All four writes switched to CONTENT_DISPOSITION (e50d237). He went further, with a guard that fails if a registered name is spelled out anywhere else (67db001). It went red on exactly those four lines before the fix (reply) A test assertion that cannot fail. django-cors-headers never echoes requested headers back, so assertNotIn("x-pilah-tidak-terdaftar", allowed) passes whatever the settings are. Only the next assertion, no *, guards anything A test should say what it actually protects Renamed as suggested, and the vacuous assertion became set equality against the allowed list, which also catches one stray header (0213cdf). He checked it fails both ways (reply)

Both suggestions were marked as nits, so they didn't block the approval. #97 merged with both changes in.

docs.title: Review given: Ghani's pilah-be #104 (PIL-248), 16 Oct
docs.text:
PIL-248 adds an operational summary to the activity feed (count, weight, deposits, payouts, period balance) and a combined Excel export of deposits and payouts. Ghani asked me and Heraldo to review. Tristan had already flagged two issues (member filter, consistent snapshot) and Gabriel one (formulas without cached values), so I reviewed the head after those fixes, without repeating their points.

Review · inline: database aggregates for the summary

The suggestion: compute the summary in the database. The feed now builds the summary on every page request, and it streams every total_nilai and nominal in the filtered range into Python to round each one down. With periode=semua that is the bank's whole history, read again on every scroll. Rounding down is Floor for non-negative amounts, so the same per-event rounding fits in Sum(Floor(...)), with the counts folded into the same queries. Before posting it, I ran a throwaway benchmark against the PR's own function (20,000 setoran and 5,000 pencairan, SQLite, best of 5):

Queries Time Result Current operational_summary 5 91 ms — Database aggregates 3 34 ms identical dict

The comment says what wasn't measured (PostgreSQL), and when Floor would differ from the current rounding: negative amounts, which a CheckConstraint could rule out. It also points out that the feed parses its filters twice, in two calls that could drift apart.

Checked and not raised. The review also records what I checked and why it isn't a finding:

  • Formula escaping. The leading apostrophe is visible in Excel. A typed text cell would hide it, but re-saving the file as CSV would then write the raw =... back out, so the current fix is the safer one.
  • The CI coverage change. I measured the coverage gate with and without tests/: 99% either way. The 80% gate already counted the test modules under apps/, so the change doesn't loosen it.
  • The durable transaction. It can't fire in production, because nothing wraps requests in atomic.

Gabriel's thread was still open, so the review is a comment, not an approval yet.

docs.title: Review received and answered: Tristan on #79, #62, #73 and #74, 11–12 Oct
docs.text:
Tristan reviewed four of my MRs on 11 Oct (and approved #92). I checked every finding against the code before changing anything; all 8 held up. Each fix went in test-first, and each thread got a reply with the commits.

MR Finding What I did Reply #79 The seed writes price versions itself, outside the approved write paths Routed it through catat_harga (dc29a68) thread #79 Rerunning the seed reprices historical setoran at today's rate Red test showed 3,500 becoming 99,999. Each setoran is now priced at its own date (857735b → f67a84f) thread #79 The filter allow-list is outside PIL-304 Reverted here and re-applied unchanged as #96, stacked on #92 thread #62 A partial save is reported as a failure The sheet now says the other fields saved and the price didn't, and stays open; retrying is safe (5a80375 → f1ea8d9) thread #62 An older list reload can overwrite a newer one Reloads are numbered and a stale answer is dropped (ece524b → bd21f70) thread #73 toInt() drops a price's sen Prices are held in sen and parsed without double (de18bfc → 4226ca5) thread #73 Versions past the first 100 disappear The history follows next to the last page (9ad13dd → 510f02a) thread #74 The Sonar exclusion still hides the DI graph, plus a merge conflict Removed the exclusion (26fcf40). Merged staging and took Tristan's identical bloc fix from #71 thread, comment

Two findings had a cheaper but worse fix that I chose not to take, and the replies say why:

  • #62, the partial save. Making the two writes atomic would need a backend endpoint that takes both. The API keeps the price separate on purpose, so that every change is a version. So the fix makes the state explicit and the retry safe instead.
  • #79, the filter split. Force-pushing #79 would have broken last week's evidence links. A revert plus cherry-pick -x keeps the history intact.

docs.title: Raising a team-wide problem: CI-built apps would crash on launch, 11 Oct
docs.text:
While covering the generated dependency graph, I found that the graph CI and CD build could not create AuthenticationBloc, which app.dart creates at start-up. It had been that way since PIL-334. The next staging APK or web build would have crashed on launch; local flutter run hid it.

  • Reproduced first. I regenerated the graph, built the bloc from it in a test, and got the exact error before reporting it.
  • Asked before touching shared code. The fix touches the team's CI and a teammate's code, so I asked how to land it, then opened #74 against staging.
  • Outcome. The same one-line fix also reached staging through Tristan's #71. #74 kept what was still new: a test that builds every registration, so this class of crash fails CI instead of the app.

docs.title: IR Part B Sprint 2 Week 2
docs.text:
Evidence for the individual review (IR), organised by competency. Each page states the competency level and the dated evidence behind it, with commit and PR links.

Part B — Hardskills: Best Practice, for Sprint 2 week 2.

What this page covers

Competency Level Status (23 Oct) Test Driven Development 4 Both fixes test-first, one behaviour per red/green pair, refactors after green; 100% of new code on SonarCloud; mocktail mocks (a fake repository behind the real cubit; captured use-case calls), viewport-driven layout tests, a proven guard, Playwright E2E through the semantics tree Programming 3 SOLID (SRP, OCP) with code blocks; Information Expert for the saldo rule; derived state instead of a stored flag; Extract Method towards command–query separation; one lock flag driving every locked field Development Discipline 3 Three MRs (#153, #154, #127), each with its own Linear issue, phase-tagged commits, detailed descriptions and green CI; follow-ups as new commits, never force-pushed; 8 approved MRs brought up to date and merged Team Development Management 3 Review of Ghani's #162, verified locally with a mutation check, with one question and two feasible suggestions; Aldo's nits checked against the code; Pascal's suggestion built test-first Code Quality 3 No open SonarCloud issue on any of the three MRs; a complexity finding on my own new code fixed by refactoring before review, not suppressed Security 1 A01 and A03 guarded and named in #127's commits (a draft link accepts only a bare id); the QA fixes have no security surface AI Literacy 3 Its claims checked against the code before acting; two of its own wrong claims corrected; a QA "Fail" traced to a deliberate rule, then fixed as the team decided; a check it could not pass reported, not worked around

Work this week:

docs.title: AI Literacy
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

AI used critically:

  • Its claims were checked against the code before anything changed.
  • Twice it said one of its own earlier claims was wrong, and changed course.
  • A QA "Fail – High" was traced to a deliberate rule before anyone called it a bug.
  • A check it could not pass was reported as such, not worked around.

Decisions with team impact were put to me and to the team: whether to warn or block, how far "survives a refresh" should go, and who reviews.

Evidence for this week:

  • Session export: Claude Code's own /export of the session behind 17–23 Oct, with tool output collapsed as the export shows it. Local home-folder paths are shortened to ~; nothing else is changed. Before publishing I checked it for tokens, keys, emails, phone numbers and teammates' Discord IDs, and found none.
  • Screenshots of the 21 Oct conversation about the QA finding on draft pencairan, below.

docs.title: How AI was used this week
docs.text:
• Tool: Claude Code as an agent in VS Code across pilah-be, pilah-mobile and pilah-docs; Linear through Composio; GitHub through gh; SonarCloud's API; Playwright against local web builds.
  • Guardrails:
    • the workspace skills (ship, tdd, multi-lgtm, ask-for-review, ask-for-qa);
    • CI's own commands, run locally before every push;
    • rules kept in memory: phase-tagged commits, 100% coverage of changed code, Playwright E2E for web UI, OWASP categories named in commits.
    • New this week:
      • I may merge my own PRs once approved (17 Oct; until then only the lead dev merged).
      • Validate any id read from a URL, after finding that go_router's push never writes to the URL.
      • agent-device, for future native-mobile E2E.
  • My role:
    • choosing PIL-341 slice 3's scope (dialogs from tablet width; a draft link that opens on its own);
    • deciding warn-not-block for the QA finding, after a team discussion;
    • refining the confirmation's list (first for several nasabah, then for every nasabah);
    • choosing reviewers;
    • granting merge permission.

docs.title: Where verification changed the outcome
docs.text: Situation What happened 17 Oct: I asked it to resolve conflicts and merge my 8 approved PRs The permission check blocked the merges. It stopped and asked, and made no attempt to get around the block. Its saved rule said the lead dev merges, so it named that conflict and let me change the rule. 17 Oct: A worktree held an unfinished merge from an earlier session It reviewed that session's conflict resolution against both sides before completing it, instead of aborting it or trusting it blindly. 17 Oct: Merging staging into PIL-341 (#83) It found that a teammate's PIL-248 (#91) had already shipped the same browser download as slice 1. It kept the teammate's version, which shares the file instead of hiding Bagikan, rather than overriding their choice. It said so in #83's description. 17 Oct: Its own temporary test copies ended up in a local merge commit It caught this before pushing and rewrote only the unpushed commits, so nothing reached GitHub. 17 Oct: Slice 3: "a saved draft survives a refresh" Its recommendation assumed the URL changes on push. While writing the test it found that go_router never writes push to the URL. It reverted the test, said its recommendation was wrong, and asked how far to go. I chose link-open only. 17 Oct: The new ?id= link It noticed that the id goes straight into request paths, so ?id=../nasabah could steer the Pengurus's own authenticated requests elsewhere. It added a guard test-first, naming OWASP A01 and A03. 21 Oct: QA "Fail – High": a Rp 50.000 Nominal paid a Rp 19 rb saldo It traced the cause to a deliberate ceiling, pinned by two tests, and said it was a missing explanation, not a calculation bug. It weighed warning against blocking, citing PIL-301's "don't fail the others", and drafted a proposal for the team. Screenshots below. 21 Oct: QA finding 2: "Edit Pencairan only lets me change keterangan" It first said the Tanggal picker still opened on a locked pencairan. While writing that test, it found an existing guard and test. It corrected itself to me, re-scoped PIL-375 to what actually confused QA (a Tanggal field that looked tappable, a note that didn't mention it), and rewrote the issue. 21 Oct: Playwright on the desktop dialog The dialog's title never reached Flutter's semantics tree, only its buttons. It logged that as INFO with a screenshot instead of marking a pass, and noted it in the PR as a likely accessibility gap in the shared dialog. 21 Oct: SonarCloud S3776 (complexity 17 of 15) The dialog had made _terapkan too complex. It extracted the confirmation into its own method as a [REFACTOR] commit, and the issue cleared. 21 Oct: Aldo's review of #153 and #154 Both nits were checked against the code before replying or merging. Both held, and neither needed a change.

docs.title: Example: a QA "Fail" that was a rule, not a bug
docs.text:
QA marked draft pencairan "Fail – High": a nasabah had about Rp 19 rb saldo, the tester set Jumlah Pencairan to Rp 50.000 and a Rp 3.000 potongan, and the draft still paid out. My first guess was a missing balance check, and I suggested a warning.

1. "Check on this finding." It did not start with my fix. It found that the tester had used the general Nominal, which is a ceiling: anyone with less saldo is paid their whole saldo. Two tests pin that on purpose, and a per-nasabah nominal above saldo is already blocked. So the bug was that nothing told the Pengurus. It agreed with a warning, and argued against blocking with the team's own PIL-301 note.

2. The team decided, then I refined it. The proposal went to the team as a doc. We chose to warn without blocking, and Pascal asked for a confirmation dialog on Terapkan. While it built that, I added a correction: list the affected nasabah when there is more than one. It took the correction mid-task and went on test-first.

3. "Even 1, and state the name." After seeing the one-nasabah dialog, I asked for the list every time. It changed the test first (red), then the code, and reran the Playwright checks for both one and two nasabah.

What changed. A "Fail – High" that looked like a missing validation became a small UX fix the team agreed on: pilah-mobile #153 (PIL-374). It shows a note under the Nominal, a confirmation that names every affected nasabah and their saldo, and a line on each capped card. The rule the tests pin stayed as it was, and the reason behind it is now on screen.

docs.title: Code Quality
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

No open SonarCloud issue on any of this week's three merge requests, and the quality gate passed on all three. Coverage on new code is 100% on each.

One issue did appear while #153 was open: a cognitive-complexity finding on code I had just written. I fixed it with a refactor before review. SonarCloud closed it, and the history shows it.

docs.title: An issue found and fixed before review
docs.text:
On 21 Oct, after the confirmation dialog and its list went into #153, SonarCloud reported:

Rule Severity Where Opened Closed dart:S3776 Cognitive Complexity Critical _terapkan in draft_editor_page.dart: "reduce its Cognitive Complexity from 17 to the 15 allowed" 21 Oct, 20:30 WIB 21 Oct, 21:24 WIB, fixed

The method had grown to hold two jobs: deciding whether to ask, and applying the settings. I did not suppress the rule or raise the threshold. The fix was an Extract Method refactor, 450bf39 (details on the Programming page):

  • _setujuSaldoKurang asks for confirmation;
  • _terapkan only applies.

The same tests stayed green, and the next analysis closed the issue as fixed. I requested reviewers only after the fix was pushed.

docs.title: Local checks before every push
docs.text:
These are the commands CI runs, run locally first on each branch:

$ dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed lib test codegen   # 0 changed
$ flutter analyze --fatal-infos                                      # no issues
$ flutter test --coverage                                            # same 25 Windows-only failures as staging, nothing new
$ diff-cover coverage/lcov.info --compare-branch=origin/staging      # 100% of changed lines

The 25 local failures are tests that compare file paths with / and so fail only on Windows: 19 of the team's design-rule tests and 6 profile-logo tests. They fail the same way on staging. To still check the design rules locally, I ran copies of all 54 design tests with Windows paths normalised to /. All pass on both branches, so neither fix adds a raw colour, font size, radius or stock widget the team's ratchets forbid.

docs.title: Development Discipline
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Three new merge requests this week, two of them the QA fixes:

  • PIL-374, the saldo warning (#153);
  • PIL-375, the locked Tanggal (#154);
  • PIL-341 slice 3, draft pencairan on a desktop window (#127, 17 Oct).

Each has its own Linear issue, a branch off staging, and scoped Conventional Commits with the TDD phase in every subject. Each also has a description with the cause, the decision, the tests, Playwright results and screenshots. CI and SonarCloud were green before each merge. All three are approved and merged.

docs.text:
MR Opened → merged Size Commits Review #153 — PIL-374: warn and confirm when a general Nominal is above a nasabah's saldo 21 Oct → 21 Oct +258 / −1, 5 files 12 approved by Aldo #154 — PIL-375: show a potongan pencairan's tanggal as locked in Edit Pencairan 21 Oct → 21 Oct +42 / −5, 3 files 2 approved by Aldo #127 — PIL-341 (3/3): draft pencairan on a desktop window 17 Oct → 18 Oct +717 / −270, 20 files 28 approved by Tristan, Pascal and Aldo

Sizes and commit counts are from GitHub on 23 Oct.

docs.title: From QA finding to merged fix
docs.text:
Both fixes went through the same steps, each recorded where the team can see it:

  1. Checked before it was called a bug. I traced each QA finding to the code. The first was a deliberate ceiling with no explanation on screen. The second was a deliberate lock that looked unlocked.
  2. The decision went to the team. For PIL-374 I wrote a short proposal: warn, block, or warn and confirm. The team chose to warn without blocking, and Pascal suggested the confirmation.
  3. Tracked in Linear. I opened PIL-374 under CPBI-22 and PIL-375 as a sub-issue of PIL-327, where the lock came from. Each has the cause, the tasks, the tests, and a note for QA. When a scope changed, I updated the issue the same day.
  4. One MR per issue, titled with the issue key so Linear links it, with a description that the reviewer can check against: what QA saw, why, what changed, the tests, the E2E results and screenshots.
  5. Review, then merge. I requested Pascal and Aldo through the team's ask-for-review skill (GitHub reviewer plus a Discord ping). I merged only after approval, with green CI and SonarCloud.

docs.title: Changes after the MR was open
docs.text:
Every change after opening #153 was a new commit, never a force-push, so the review history stays readable:

  • Pascal's suggestion, a confirmation on Terapkan: a red/green pair.
  • My request to list the affected nasabah: a red/green pair.
  • SonarCloud S3776: a [REFACTOR] commit.

The description was rewritten each time, so it always matched the head commit.

docs.title: Also this week: the Sprint 2 merges (17 Oct)
docs.text:
My 8 approved MRs from Sprint 2 had fallen behind staging, and 5 had conflicts. I resolved each on its own branch, by merging staging in rather than force-pushing:

docs.title: Programming
docs.text:
Competency level: 3

Standard principles applied and shown in the two QA fixes:

  • SOLID: single responsibility and open/closed. See SOLID in this week's code.
  • Information Expert: the "is this nasabah short?" rule lives next to the ceiling it describes.
  • A derived flag computed from state, never stored.
  • Command–query separation, reached through an Extract Method refactor.
  • One lock flag driving every locked field through the same enabled convention.

Each item names the design issue it addresses, the pattern or principle used, its type and where the issue came from.

docs.title: Design issues and the patterns that address them
docs.text:
Code Design issue Pattern / principle Type Origin melebihiSaldo Duplicated business rule: the screen needs "is this nasabah short?", and recomputing it in the UI would duplicate hitung's ceiling, so the two could drift Information Expert (GRASP): JumlahUmum, which owns the ceiling, answers the question Principle (GRASP) Designed in (PIL-374) dibatasiSaldo Stale state: a stored "capped" flag would go out of date the moment the pengurus types a nominal Derived state / single source of truth: a query method computes it from the applied Nominal and the item Technique (derived state) Designed in (PIL-374) _setujuSaldoKurang Long method mixing a question with an action: _terapkan both built the confirmation and applied the settings, at cognitive complexity 17 of 15 Extract Method (Fowler) towards command–query separation: one method answers "may this be applied?", the other applies Refactoring + principle Tool finding on my own code (SonarCloud S3776) isi: slot Changing a shared dialog to add one caller's content Open/closed via composition: showPencairanKonfirmasi already takes an isi widget, so the list is passed in and the dialog is unchanged Principle (SOLID OCP) Designed in (PIL-374) enabled Inconsistent locked state: one flag (_terkunci) disabled the Nominal, while the Tanggal only ignored taps and still looked active One flag through a uniform interface: the field takes enabled, as Material's own fields do, and _terkunci drives both Technique (consistency) QA finding (PIL-375)

The GoF patterns these changes sit on are listed in GoF design patterns in this week's code.

docs.title: The rule lives with the ceiling — 0511e1b
docs.text:
hitung already caps a fixed rupiah at the saldo. The question "will this nasabah get less than asked?" is the same rule seen from the other side, so it sits right below it, in the same class:

lib/features/draft_pencairan/domain/model/draft_pencairan.dart
int hitung(int saldo) {
  switch (jenis) {
    case JumlahJenis.persen:
      return _persenDari(saldo, nilai);
    case JumlahJenis.rupiah:
      final tetap = nilai.floor();
      return tetap < saldo ? tetap : saldo;
  }
}

/// Whether a nasabah with [saldo] gets less than this asks for: a fixed
/// rupiah above their saldo, so [hitung] pays them their whole saldo.
bool melebihiSaldo(int saldo) =>
    jenis == JumlahJenis.rupiah && valid && nilai.floor() > saldo;

The note under the field, the confirmation, its list and each card's line all ask melebihiSaldo. None of them compares amounts itself. The reviewer checked the edge case: a saldo exactly equal to the Nominal is paid in full, and isn't warned about.

docs.title: A derived flag, not a stored one — bcde54e
Asking and applying, split — 450bf39
docs.text:
SonarCloud flagged _terapkan (S3776, complexity 17 of 15) once it held both the confirmation and the apply. Extracting the question gives each method one job:

lib/features/draft_pencairan/presentation/pages/draft_editor_page.dart
/// True when there is nothing to confirm or the pengurus says yes.
Future<bool> _setujuSaldoKurang(JumlahUmum? jumlah) async {
  final kurang = _jumlahKurang(jumlah);
  if (jumlah == null || kurang == 0) return true;
  return showPencairanKonfirmasi(
    context,
    icon: Icons.warning_amber_rounded,
    judul: 'Terapkan Nominal ${rupiah(jumlah.nilai.floor())}?',
    pesan: _pesanKurang(kurang, jumlah),
    isi: _DaftarSaldoKurang(
      items: [
        for (final item in _items)
          if (jumlah.melebihiSaldo(item.saldo)) item,
      ],
    ),
    jawaban: const KonfirmasiJawaban('Ya, terapkan'),
    nada: KonfirmasiNada.peringatan,
  );
}

Future<void> _terapkan() async {
  final jumlah = _jumlahBerubah ? _jumlah : null;
  if (!await _setujuSaldoKurang(jumlah) || !mounted) return;
  context.read<DraftEditorCubit>().terapkanUmum(
        metode: _metodeBerubah ? _metode : null,
        jumlah: jumlah,
        potongan: _potonganBerubah ? _potongan : null,
      );
  // …
}

The behaviour didn't change, and the same tests stayed green. SonarCloud closed the issue on the next analysis.

docs.title: The dialog extended, not edited — b5c6b79
docs.text: The confirmation is the shared showPencairanKonfirmasi, which already accepts an isi widget between its message and its buttons. The list of affected nasabah, with name and saldo, is a small _DaftarSaldoKurang widget passed into that slot. The dialog function is untouched. The other screens that use it (konfirmasi pembayaran, batalkan, buang perubahan) can't be affected.

docs.text:
Edit Pencairan already had one rule for "this pencairan's amount and date are fixed": _terkunci => potongan > 0. It disabled the Nominal field, but the Tanggal only had a guard inside its tap handler, so it still looked editable. Now the same flag drives both, through the same enabled parameter Material's fields use:

lib/features/pencairan/presentation/widgets/pencairan_form_fields.dart
InkWell(
  key: const Key('tanggal-field'),
  onTap: enabled ? onTap : null,
  child: InputDecorator(
    decoration: appInputDecoration(
      suffixIcon: const Icon(Icons.calendar_month, color: AppColors.grey100),
      errorText: errorText,
    ).copyWith(enabled: enabled),
    // …
lib/features/pencairan/presentation/pages/edit_pencairan_page.dart
TanggalPencairanField(
  tanggal: _tanggal,
  onTap: _pickTanggal,
  errorText: state.fieldErrors['tanggal'],
  enabled: !_terkunci,
),

enabled defaults to true, so the field's existing callers are unchanged.

docs.title: SOLID in this week's code
docs.text: Principle Where How Single responsibility _setujuSaldoKurang / _terapkan One method decides whether to proceed (and asks), the other applies. Each changes for one reason. Open/closed showPencairanKonfirmasi(isi:), TanggalPencairanField(enabled:) New behaviour arrives through a slot and a defaulted parameter. The shared dialog and the field's existing uses are not modified. Dependency inversion (kept) The editor's cubit The saldo checks are plain domain methods. The cubit still depends on the DraftPencairanRepository interface, which is why the tests mock it.

docs.title: GoF design patterns in this week's code
docs.text:
• Observer: the cubit emits states and BlocBuilder rebuilds the editor. That is how the note, the cards and the totals follow the applied Nominal without being told.
  • Strategy: showPencairanKonfirmasi goes through showAdaptiveConfirmation, which picks the presentation (a sheet on a phone, a dialog in a browser) from the window width. The caller's code is the same either way.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Competency level: 1

This week's work guards and names two OWASP Top 10 categories in its commits, A01 Broken Access Control and A03 Injection. Both come from one guard in PIL-341 slice 3 (#127, 17 Oct).

The two QA fixes are UI changes with no security surface, so I don't claim anything for them. Level 2 needs at least five categories named in commits, and level 3 a scan with a patch plan; this week has neither. The Metasploit scan and its patch plan were claimed in Sprint 2 Week 1 and aren't counted again.

docs.title: OWASP guards in this week's code
docs.text: OWASP category Guard Commits Named in the commit A01 Broken Access Control A draft link only opens a bare draft id, so a crafted link can't steer the pengurus's own authenticated requests to another endpoint a491758 → 7d938f9 yes A03 Injection The same guard: input from the URL is never pasted into a request path unless it is a bare id the same pair yes

docs.title: A01 and A03: the draft link
docs.text:
PIL-341 slice 3 lets a saved draft open from /draft-pencairan/editor?id=<draftId>. The editor builds its requests by appending that id to a path:

  • GET draft-pencairan/<id>
  • PATCH the same path
  • POST draft-pencairan/<id>/konfirmasi and POST draft-pencairan/<id>/batalkan

So a crafted link such as ?id=../nasabah or ?id=d-1%2Fkonfirmasi would have sent the Pengurus's own authenticated requests to a path the editor never meant to call. That is user input injected into a request path (A03), used to reach past the intended access path with the victim's credentials (A01).

The guard, 7d938f9: DraftEditorArgs.fromRoute accepts an id from a link only if it matches ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$, the shape of a UUID or a slug. Anything else sends the user to the draft list.

The test, red first, a491758: it visits ?id=..%2Fnasabah, ?id=d-1%2Fkonfirmasi and ?id=%20. For each it asserts that the user lands on the draft list, and that no request to a draft path is built from the link. It failed before the guard, because the editor opened.

Checked end to end. A Playwright run against a local build and backend confirmed it: ?id=..%2Fnasabah lands on the list on desktop and phone, and a real UUID still opens its draft.

docs.title: Test Driven Development
docs.text:
Competency level: 4

Level 3 met: both QA fixes were built test-first, one behaviour per [RED] → [GREEN] pair, with the phase in every commit subject and [REFACTOR] commits after green. Every changed line is covered (100% on SonarCloud for both MRs). The tests cover the positive case, the negative case (nothing shown or applied) and the corner cases (exactly one affected nasabah, Persen instead of Nominal, a hand-typed nominal).

Level 4: advanced testing methods in the commits:

  • Mocks for isolation:
  • Viewport-driven tests: the test view is resized to phone and desktop, so one test drives each adaptive layout.
  • Proven guards: a test that passed when written is shown to guard its code, and a changed test is shown red before the code follows.
  • E2E through Flutter's semantics tree: Playwright, at desktop and phone sizes, against a local build and backend.

docs.title: 153's tests run the real DraftEditorCubit on a mocktail _MockRepository, a fake DraftPencairanRepository, so no server is involved and the tests assert what the cubit holds.
154's tests use a mocked PencairanUseCases, and verify(… captureAny()) captures the request to check that a locked pencairan still sends its nominal and tanggal exactly as recorded.
Coverage proof at a glance
docs.text:
MR Work SonarCloud new-code coverage Local diff coverage pilah-mobile #153 PIL-374: saldo warning and confirmation 100% of 56 lines, screenshot 100% of 56 changed lines pilah-mobile #154 PIL-375: locked Tanggal 100% of 5 lines, screenshot 100% of 5 changed lines

docs.title: PIL-374: warn when a general Nominal is above a nasabah's saldo — pilah-mobile #153
docs.text:
The QA finding was "a Rp 50.000 Nominal paid a Rp 19 rb saldo". The ceiling that does that is intended and stays. These tests make it visible.

Behaviour Red Green A note under the Nominal says how many nasabah it holds to their saldo: none at Rp 40.000, one at Rp 100.000, none for Persen; Terapkan stays enabled 3794f95 0511e1b After Terapkan, only the capped nasabah's card says "Saldo tidak cukup untuk …"; a hand-typed nominal clears it b99dff3 bcde54e Terapkan asks first; Batal applies nothing, "Ya, terapkan" applies 86427cb 416ac45 The confirmation lists the affected nasabah by name and saldo, and only them b49e031 b5c6b79 Review feedback: list them even when there is only one 6e5b9d5 d90af9d

Refactor after green:

  • 42dd487 put a doc comment back on the method it describes.
  • 450bf39 extracted the confirmation from _terapkan, after SonarCloud flagged its complexity (Code Quality). The same tests stayed green.

Each red failed for the right reason:

  • The note test failed on "no element" (no note yet).
  • The dialog test failed on the missing title "Terapkan Nominal Rp 100.000?".
  • The one-nasabah list test failed on "found 0 widgets with text Budi Santoso".

These runs are in the session export.

Proven guards. "A Nominal every saldo covers applies without asking" went in with the dialog's red commit and passed from the start. It is a guard: it fails if the dialog ever shows when nobody is short.

Positive, negative and corner cases: see the table below.

Existing tests kept on the real flow. The shared _terapkanUmum helper now confirms the dialog when it appears, so older tests that apply Rp 100.000 still go through it. They don't bypass it.

docs.title: PIL-375: show a potongan pencairan's Tanggal as locked — pilah-mobile #154
docs.text:
Behaviour Red Green For a pencairan with a potongan, the Tanggal field is disabled (InputDecorator.decoration.enabled == false) with no onTap, and the note names both locked fields 69e50ce 6e15f8c

What the tests assert. They check the widget's own state, the disabled decoration and the nulled tap handler. A text lookup alone would pass even if the field still looked tappable.

Negative case, kept from the existing suite: a pencairan without a potongan still opens the date picker (see the table below).

An honest note on this one. While planning the fix, I first assumed the picker still opened on a locked pencairan. Writing the red test showed an existing guard (_pickTanggal returns early) and an existing test for it. So the issue was re-scoped to what QA actually saw, a field that looked tappable, before any code changed.

docs.title: Positive, negative and corner cases
docs.text:
The examples use the editor tests' three nasabah: Ahmad (saldo Rp 465.600), Budi (Rp 50.000) and Citra (Rp 250.000).

Behaviour Positive Negative Corner Note under the general Nominal (#153) Rp 100.000: "1 nasabah saldonya di bawah Rp 100.000. Mereka dicairkan seluruh saldonya." Rp 40.000, which every saldo covers: no note Persen: no note, because a share never exceeds a saldo Confirmation on Terapkan (#153) Rp 100.000 asks first; "Ya, terapkan" applies ([100000, 50000, 100000]) Batal applies nothing ([465600, 50000, 250000]); Rp 40.000 applies without asking — List in the confirmation (#153) Rp 300.000 lists Budi and Citra, each with "Saldo Rp …" Ahmad, whose saldo covers it, is not listed Exactly one nasabah affected (Rp 100.000): Budi is still listed, Citra isn't Line on each capped card (#153) Budi's card: "Saldo tidak cukup untuk Rp 100.000, dicairkan Rp 50.000" Ahmad's and Citra's cards: no line A nominal typed by hand on Budi's card clears his line Locked Tanggal (#154) A pencairan with a potongan: Tanggal disabled with no onTap, and the note names nominal and tanggal A pencairan without a potongan: Tanggal still opens the date picker A locked pencairan still saves a metode change, sending its nominal and tanggal exactly as recorded (checked through the captured use-case call)

Run on 21 Oct against flutter build web --profile and a local backend seeded with seed_testing_data, at 1440×900 and 390×844. The checks are driven through Flutter's semantics tree, wait on labels and assert outcomes. The results and screenshots are in #153 and #154.
